title: Generate createdAt client-side and share timestamps across MTI inserts
body:
## Linked issue

n/a — Linear reference omitted as requested.

## At a glance

```prisma
model Reading {
  id             Int    @id
  label          String
  createdAt      temporal.createdAt()
  updatedAt      temporal.updatedAt()
  createdAtText  temporal.createdAtString()
  updatedAtText  temporal.updatedAtString()
  @@map("reading")
}
```

These existing presets now generate both timestamps client-side; previously `createdAt` used the database clock.

## Summary

Make creation and update timestamp presets use the same clock, including when one multi-table inheritance (MTI) create requires separate base-table and variant-table inserts.

## Decision

1. Generate `createdAt` and `createdAtString` on create using the same execution generators as their corresponding update presets. Only `updatedAt` regenerates on non-empty updates.
2. Share one query-stable generator cache across every table and row in an MTI create operation. Separate calls retain independent caches; field-stable ID generators remain independent.

## Notes for the reviewer

- Explicit `@default(now())` remains database-generated. This changes the convenience presets, not SQL `now()` lowering.
- Existing users of creation presets must re-emit contracts and reconcile database defaults through migration. Once the default is removed, direct SQL writers must supply the timestamp themselves.
- Equality applies to matching generator/representation pairs, not across Temporal and string representations using different generators.
- MTI regression tests verify shared cache identity and isolation between operations; the runtime suite separately verifies query-stable reuse and field-stable independence.
- The full fixture check timed out after regenerating the affected integration fixture; it is not reported as passing.

## How it fits together

1. The shared SQL preset factory emits an `onCreate` generator instead of a storage default.
2. PostgreSQL selects `instantNow` for Temporal presets and `timestampNow` for string presets; SQLite uses its existing generator.
3. MTI orchestration creates a cache before iterating rows and passes it through both inserts.
4. Authoring mirrors, parity tests, documentation, and emitted integration contracts reflect the new defaults.

## Behavior changes & evidence

- **Creation timestamps use the client clock and match corresponding initial update timestamps.** Implemented in [the preset factory](packages/2-sql/9-family/src/core/timestamp-now-generator.ts); covered by [preset tests](packages/2-sql/9-family/test/temporal-codec-presets.test.ts) and [database integration tests](test/integration/test/temporal-defaults/temporal-defaults.integration.test.ts), including unchanged creation timestamps after updates.
- **MTI inserts share query-stable defaults across tables and bulk rows.** Implemented in [collection orchestration](packages/3-extensions/sql-orm-client/src/collection.ts); covered by [MTI regressions](packages/3-extensions/sql-orm-client/test/collection-variant.test.ts) and [runtime cache tests](packages/2-sql/5-runtime/test/sql-context.test.ts).

## Testing performed

- `pnpm --dir packages/3-extensions/sql-orm-client test` — 918 passed, no type errors.
- `pnpm --dir packages/2-sql/9-family test` — 329 passed.
- `pnpm --dir packages/2-sql/2-authoring/contract-psl test` — 474 passed.
- `pnpm --dir packages/2-sql/5-runtime test test/sql-context.test.ts` — 26 passed.
- PostgreSQL and SQLite authoring-field-presets suites — 23 and 6 passed.
- `pnpm --dir test/integration test test/temporal-defaults/temporal-defaults.integration.test.ts` — 2 passed, no type errors.
- Package typechecks passed for SQL ORM client, SQL family, SQL contract PSL, and PostgreSQL target.
- PostgreSQL public-facade/native-type parity suites — 47 passed; PostgreSQL extension typecheck passed.
- `pnpm check:upgrade-coverage --mode pr --prev 2a30eb193d78362cec40c36ea7bc226dce5da231 --head HEAD` — passed after adding upgrade fragments.
- Biome checks and focused dependency checks passed at commit time.
- `pnpm fixtures:check:agent` — timed out after 300 seconds; the affected fixture was regenerated and its integration tests passed afterward.

## Skill update

Upgrade fragments describe [application contract/default migration](upgrade-instructions/pending/client-generated-created-at/app/instructions.md) and [extension cache sharing](upgrade-instructions/pending/client-generated-created-at/extension/instructions.md). Package authoring references and the runtime error reference document the changed clock/default behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) per the DCO.
- [x] I read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the change is scoped to one logical concern.
- [x] Tests are updated.
- [ ] The PR title is in `TML-NNNN: <sentence-case title>` form — intentionally omitted at the author's request.
- [x] The **Skill update** section is filled in.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep creation timestamps database-generated: rejected because creation and update presets would still use different clocks.
- Generate defaults separately for each MTI insert: rejected because splitting one logical operation would change its timestamp values.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Timestamp helpers now generate client-side values on create instead of database storage defaults.
  - `updatedAt()` generates timestamps on create and non-empty updates.
  - Matching timestamp representations share one generated value per operation, including multi-table creates.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Corrected timestamp consistency across related inserts and updates.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated timestamp behavior, migration guidance, runtime requirements, and error references to reflect client-side generation.
